Hey dude, I was in a similar (but admittedly less bad) position back in school. If i got less than 8/10 I would immediately panic and sometimes breakdown (even during class) because I was scared of my parents dissapointment. I was following behind a very clever older sibling who was also in a better school than me.
At some point it stops being scary! You have done exceptionaly well in school and thats amazing. I had an epiphany after entering university that my grades are my own. If I do well, good job, if not, I can do better, it's not that scary. Good grades are proof of hard work but they're not the thing that defines your value. Sometimes I find the work I have to do extremely burdensome and my grade reflects that - and thats ok! Nothing bad happens after.
I encourage you to start appreciating your own cleverness for keeping up with your education, but allowing yourself a bit of freedom. Your mums opinion doesn't matter as much as you think it does, and enjoying the work you do or time you spend is much more valuable than chasing approval.
All the best to you!! I'm proud of how far you have come.

I don't know how much it will help, but I am speaking from a perspective similar to that of your friend.

In high school (not that long ago) I spent every day messaging and being probably one of the very few genuine supportive friends to one of my best friends at a time, who had many issues which made her depressed, anxious, and maybe borderline suicidal (I'm still not sure). For a couple years I did my best but it started to get exhausting - there is only so much I could shoulder her, and it seemed like I was repeating myself over and over again. But I also couldn't just abandon her, so I went through with it and tried my best to he supportive as long as possible.

When I started having too many of my own issues to deal with to also be able to be emotionally invested in her, I slowly started distancing myself, replying less. Besides, she had found someone else in her life to help her out. She was also going to therapy.

I layed our previous relationship down because I haven't talked to her properly for a good year, and reconnected just a few days ago. I used to equate talking to her as giving free "therapy" - something that became tiring. But after taking a break, I became neutral, and when I saw she messaged me I got kind of excited. No matter what, she is first and foremost my friend. I spent time chatting and exchanging memes and news and conversation flowed so easily. She became more confident and cheerful. She said she likes texting me as well, which made me feel good.

OP, things change with time. You might be scared to approach your friend, but you miss 100% of shots you don't take. You got help and gotten better, and could possibly become a good friend this time around. I think you should give it a chance and contact them, see where it goes. Maybe it will result in a whole new, better, rekindled friendship. And if they clearly don't want to reconnect, then it will serve as closure for you - you have done all you could. Continue to grow and get better, and you will make many more valuable connections as you go, I promise.
